HDB-SQI is a transparent research-prototype index, not a validated clinical score. It combines duration (35%), sleep efficiency (30%), sleep latency (15%), WASO (10%), number of awakenings (5%) and subjective quality (5%). Personal deviation remains a separate within-person metric.

Blood Baseline

Store laboratory values measured when you consider yourself in your usual, well state. Use the units shown or leave a field blank.

Important: this module builds your personal longitudinal distribution; it does not diagnose disease and does not replace the laboratory reference interval. Different laboratories, methods, age and sex can affect reference ranges.

Format: analyte key | unit | lower limit | upper limit. Saved with that blood draw so laboratory-specific ranges are never confused with your personal baseline.

LONGITUDINAL FUNCTION

Neuro Function Log

Track changes in memory, gait, motor function, daily function and selected non-motor features over time.

Not an Alzheimer/Parkinson diagnostic test. These features are nonspecific and can have many causes. The purpose is longitudinal change detection and correlation with the independent cognitive battery.

Observation window: past 7 daysFor non-countable symptoms, record on how many days the symptom was present: 0 = 0 days; 1 = 1–2 days; 2 = 3–4 days; 3 = 5–7 days. Falls and trips/near-falls remain exact numeric counts.

Operational definitions — always use the same criteria

FallCount 1 event when you unintentionally come to rest on the ground, floor, or another lower level. Exact count.
Trip / near-fallCount 1 event when balance is lost or you trip but recover without reaching the ground or a lower level. Exact count.
Recent-memory lapsePositive day if recent information/event is forgotten and a reminder or repetition is needed.
Word findingPositive day if a familiar word cannot be retrieved and must be replaced, described, or supplied.
Missed task/appointmentPositive day if a planned activity is forgotten without an external reminder.
Misplaced objectPositive day if an everyday object is put in an unexpected place and its location cannot be promptly retraced.
PlanningPositive day if a familiar multi-step activity needs help, repetition, or more attempts than usual.
DisorientationPositive day if date, place, or familiar route is mistaken and correction or guidance is required.
Conversation / readingPositive day if the thread is lost and rereading or repetition is required for comprehension.
Motor slownessPositive day if a familiar motor activity is clearly slower than personal usual performance.
StiffnessPositive day if stiffness changes at least one usual movement or activity.
TremorPositive day if visible tremor occurs at rest or during an action, excluding external vibration.
Fine motorPositive day if buttons, handwriting, or another fine-motor task takes more attempts or time than usual.
Gait changePositive day if shorter steps, dragging, or another evident gait change occurs versus personal usual.
Freezing-likePositive day if, while intending to start or continue walking, the feet temporarily seem unable to initiate movement.
Chair risePositive day if more attempts, new arm use, or assistance is required versus usual.
SmellPositive day if familiar odors normally perceived are clearly less noticeable under comparable conditions.
Constipation changePositive day if bowel pattern differs from personal usual; record obvious context factors in Context Log.
Sleep movement/vocalizationPositive day only when reported by an observer or recalled as motor/vocal behavior during sleep.
Daytime sleepinessPositive day if unintended sleepiness occurs during an activity normally performed awake.
Standing light-headednessPositive day if dizziness/faintness follows standing; orthostatic blood pressure remains separate in Vitals.
Urinary urgency/frequencyPositive day only for a new change versus personal usual baseline.
SwallowingPositive day if food/liquid causes coughing, sticking sensation, or repeated swallowing attempts.
Softer voicePositive day if self or observer notices a softer-than-usual voice under comparable conditions.
Daily activitiesPositive day if a usual personal/household activity needs new assistance or is not completed as usual.
Driving / navigationPositive day if a new error occurs on a familiar route or navigation task.
InitiativePositive day if a usual planned activity is not initiated despite time and opportunity.
Mood / behaviorPositive day only for an observable change versus personal usual, reported by self or observer.
Visual perceptionsPositive day if a person/object/animal is clearly reported as seen despite not being present; this is not a diagnosis.

Rule: Common rule: for symptoms, count positive days, not total episodes within a day. Use 0, 1–2, 3–4, or 5–7 days. Falls and near-falls remain exact event counts.

INTERPRETATION GUIDE

Which longitudinal changes can be seen in neurodegenerative disease?

RESEARCH CONTEXT

These directions are literature-informed associations, not diagnostic thresholds. A persistent change may also reflect fatigue, sleep loss, stress, pain, medication, illness, practice, device differences, hand position or normal day-to-day variability. HDB therefore interprets patterns only against the participant's own standardized longitudinal baseline.

↓ Tapping speed What HDB sees

Fewer taps per second, especially when the reduction persists across standardized sessions.

Research meaning: slowing can be compatible with bradykinesia. Longitudinal smartphone research in Parkinson disease has reported reduced tapping speed over follow-up, although speed alone did not reliably distinguish PD from controls at baseline.
↑ Inter-tap variability What HDB sees

Higher ITI CV: the rhythm becomes less regular from tap to tap.

Research meaning: increased tapping dysrhythmia has been reported in Parkinson disease and also in MCI/Alzheimer cohorts. It is informative but nonspecific.
↑ Right-left asymmetry What HDB sees

A growing difference in tapping rate between the two hands relative to the person's usual asymmetry.

Research meaning: Parkinson motor manifestations commonly begin asymmetrically. Digital tapping studies have also found larger bilateral tapping differences in PD groups. Hand dominance must be considered.
↓ Performance during the trial What HDB sees

Second-half rate falls relative to the first half and/or the five-bin speed slope becomes more negative.

Research meaning: progressive reduction in speed is related to the motor “sequence effect” studied in parkinsonian bradykinesia. HDB measures temporal speed decrement, not clinical finger-thumb amplitude decrement.
↑ Pauses / hesitations What HDB sees

More unusually long inter-tap intervals relative to the person's own within-trial rhythm.

Research meaning: interruptions and rhythm breakdown are relevant to bradykinetic tapping assessment, but HDB's long-ITI rule is an original research proxy and is not a validated clinical cutoff.
Motor + cognitive change What HDB sees

Persistent motor changes occur together with slower/more variable reaction time, lower memory-check/recall performance or reduced inhibition accuracy.

Research meaning: cognitive impairment can occur in neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson disease and dementias. A multidomain pattern is more informative for research than one isolated tapping value, but remains non-diagnostic.
What would make an HDB pattern more noteworthy? Persistence across repeated standardized sessions + simultaneous worsening in several independent features + change larger than the person's usual variability. There is currently no HDB percentage, tapping value or Motor Pattern Score that establishes Parkinson disease, MCI or Alzheimer disease.
Evidence basis: WHO Parkinson disease fact sheet; Marsili et al., J Neurol Sci 2024 (PMID 39033737); Roalf et al., J Neurol 2018 (PMID 29619565); Hasan et al., BRAIN Tap Test sequence-effect study (PMID 31392247). Feature directions are used for research interpretation only.

How the Motor Pattern Score works. The 0–100 score is a transparent within-person research index, not a disease probability. It combines six equally weighted tapping features: mean rate ↓, inter-tap variability ↑, right-left asymmetry ↑, second-half slowing ↓, progressive speed slope ↓, and pauses/hesitations ↑. Each feature is standardized against that participant's prior robust baseline using median and MAD. Adverse deviation magnitude is mapped from 0 to 100 and capped at 3 robust SD-equivalents; the displayed persistence count separately requires the last two observations to be ≥1.5 robust z in the same adverse direction. Pointer pressure is deliberately excluded because it is hardware/browser dependent.

STANDARDIZATION

Profile & Protocol

Minimal information used to improve longitudinal comparability. Stored locally in this browser.

Preferred cognitive protocol

v6.2.3 full QA fix. A cold-load audit found that both Overview and Data Collection were initially visible because the Home section lacked its initial hidden state. Home now starts hidden, Overview is the sole initial screen, and About/Home navigation also uses the same primary-screen router. This is a UI-only fix; protocols and scoring are unchanged.
v6.2.2 hardened navigation. Pre-test routing now uses one explicit primary-screen controller and .hidden is enforced with !important. This prevents Overview/Data Collection layout rules from remaining visible over an instruction or test screen on Safari/iPad. The three entry points and the post-save return use the same router. Test protocols and scoring are unchanged.
v6.2.1 navigation fix. Corrected the primary-screen selector so Data Collection is actually hidden when a test instruction screen opens, and restored deterministic return to Data Collection after saving a completed test. This is a UI bugfix; test protocols and scoring are unchanged.
Test flow v6.2. Cognitive, Tapping and Memory modules now open a dedicated instruction screen before any timed or scored task begins. No timer or stimulus starts until the participant presses START. On completion, the session is saved and HDB returns directly to Data Collection with a confirmation banner.
Memory Check v6.1 form. This module is deliberately a brief longitudinal cognitive check rather than an intelligence-style test. It contains four routine items (4-digit forward, 5-digit forward ×2, 4-digit reverse), followed by two explicit recall items (4-digit recall and 6-digit recall), then two challenge items (7-digit forward and 6-digit reverse). HDB reports routine 0–4, recall 0–2, core check + recall 0–6, challenge 0–2 and total 0–8 separately. The neurodegenerative research layer uses the core check + recall score and excludes challenge items. For formal longitudinal work, use the same v6.1 protocol consistently; do not directly pool it with earlier WMI forms.
Tapping 2.1 research basis. The bilateral test stores raw tap timestamps and derives rate, every inter-tap interval, interval variability, first-vs-second-half change, pause/hesitation proxies, five-bin progressive speed slope and right-left asymmetry. When the browser exposes genuinely variable PointerEvent pressure, HDB also stores it as an exploratory device-dependent channel. MDS-UPDRS clinical finger tapping evaluates speed, rhythm interruptions and amplitude decrement; HDB can quantify timing; PointerEvent pressure is not equivalent to finger-thumb movement amplitude, so amplitude is not claimed without a validated camera/sensor method. Research examples: PMID 29619565, PMID 39033737, PMID 37694362, PMID 39920091. These studies support feature selection, not diagnostic thresholds.

v6.2.3 Motor Pattern Score: six tapping features are equally weighted after within-person robust standardization. For each feature, only deviation in the predefined adverse direction contributes: component = clamp(adverse robust z / 3, 0, 1) × 100. The six available components are averaged. Persistence is reported separately and requires the last two observations to be at least 1.5 robust z in the same adverse direction. The score is not calibrated to Parkinson disease, Alzheimer disease, MCI, prevalence, sensitivity or specificity. The neurodegenerative research section displays every motor component separately with latest value, robust personal-baseline median, change from baseline, adverse robust-z, 0–100 component contribution and persistence state. It also includes a literature-informed interpretation guide explaining which directions of change have been reported in neurodegenerative research and why none of them constitutes a diagnostic threshold.
